newsitem.title: USA: FDA panels backs new use for Amgen's Neupogen.
newsitem.headline: FDA panels backs new use for Amgen's Neupogen.

text.p: BETHESDA, Md., July 25, Reuter - A U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) advisory panel on Friday voted 15-0 that Amgen Inc's Filgrastim (Neupogen) is effective for reduction of fever and neutropenia -- depressed white blood cell count -- in induction and consolidation chemotherapy for Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML).
The product practically breezed through the panel despite minor safety concerns, particularly regarding some events of hemorrhaging.
The FDA is not bound by its panels' advice, but usually follows it.

Amgen presented data from a single, large pivotal phase III trial of Neupogen for initial intensive chemotherapy (induction) and a smaller supportive study in patients undergoing a second round (consolidation).
In the induction study, conducted in Europe and Australia from 1992-95, 262 patients were given placebo and 290 patients were given Neupogen, six days after beginning chemotherapy.
All patients were treated in the hospital and given quinolone antibiotics as a preventive therapy.

Amgen said that Neupogen reduced duration of neutropenia, noting that placebo patients had neutropenia an average 19 days compared to 14 for Neupogen patients. Similar results were seen in the consolidation study, said Amgen.
